question: The Young Bengal Movement was founded by ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __Henry Louis Vivian Derozio__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Henry Louis Vivian Derozio__ is the founder of the Young Bengal movement.
 
• Henry Louis Vivian Derozio: 
 __
 
• He was an Indian poet of Portuguese origin and assistant headmaster of Hindu College, Kolkata.
 
• He was a radical thinker of his time and one of the first Indian educators to disseminate Western learning and science among the young men of Bengal.
 
• He joined the Hindu College as a teacher at the age of seventeen.
 
• He and his students called DErozians or Young Bengal promoted radical reformist ideas among the people of Bengal. 
 
• He was a poet, novelist, and writer. He was also the first nationalist poet of modern India.
 
• The " Fakeer of Jungheera" is a long poem by Henry Louis Vivian Derozio.
 
• Most of the work in found to Indian religion, culture, rule and regulation, rigidity, culture, etc.
 
• Derozio died of cholera at an early age of 22 on 26 December 1831 in Calcutta. His body was buried in the South Park Street Cemetery of Kolkata.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Dayananda Saraswati

 
 
• Dayananda Saraswati [1824-1883] was the first to give the call for Swarajya – "India for Indians" – in 1876.
 
• For his own inspiration, Swami Dayanand went to the Vedas which he regarded as infallible.
 
• He rejected all later religious thought if it conflicted with the Vedas.
 
• This total dependence on Vedas and their infallibility gave his teachings orthodox coloring.
 
• He was opposed to idolatry, ritual, and priesthood and particularly to the prevalent caste practices and popular Hinduism as preached by brahmins.
 
• ​Swami Dayanand met Keshub Chandra Sen, Vidyasagar, Justice Ranade, Gopal Hari Deshmukh, and other modern religious and social reformers.
 
• He took inspiration from the Vedas and considered them to be ‘India’s Rock of Ages, the infallible, and the true original seed of Hinduism. 
 
• He gave the slogan “Back to the Vedas”.
 
• Dayananda’s slogan of ‘Back to the Vedas’ was a call for a revival of Vedic learning and Vedic purity of religion and not a revival of Vedic times.
 
• He accepted modernity and displayed a patriotic attitude to national problems.
 
 
 
• Lala Hansraj
 
 
• ​Anglo-Vedic colleges or schools are also known as Dayanand Anglo-Vedic schools.
 
• Dayanand Anglo Vedic (DAV) Schools were founded in 1886 in Lahore by the efforts of Mahatma Hansraj in memory of Swami Dayanand Saraswati.
 
• The schools were run by the Dayanand Anglo-Vedic College Trust & Management Society, also known as the Dayanand Anglo-Vedic Education Society.
 
• DAV institutions are the best place to study and work together.
 
• Under the DAV family, there are 900 schools, 75 colleges, and a university.
 
• “DAV Movement” founded in 1886 by Lala Lajpat Rai (Father of the DAV Movement) picked up momentum due to the arduous efforts of Lala Lajpat Rai, Mahatma Hans Raj, Pandit Gurudutt Vidyarthi, and many others dedicated as the Arya Samaj activist. 
 
 
 
• Keshub Chandra Sen (also spelled Keshab Chunder Sen) was born in an affluent family of Calcutta on 19 November 1838.
 
 
• In 1857, he joined the Brahmo Samaj and took up studying philosophy.
 
• Sen was inspired by Christian teachings and sought to fuse Christian teachings into the Hindu framework.
 
• He thought that only the Christian doctrine would help instill new life into Hindu society.
 
• He was also impressed with the discipline of Christian missionary work and started following it himself.
 
• His lean towards Christianity caused a rift between him and Tagore and he broke away from the Samaj and formed the Bharat Barshiya Brahmo Samaj (Brahmo Samaj of India).
